# sv0c native runtime executable output: slice backlog

## purpose

The trackable **`NEX-###`** slice backlog for the native-executable-output
feature specified at `~/Documents/project-specs/sv0c-runtime-executable/SPEC.md`
§31. The **definition of done**, scope decisions, release ladder, and gates
live in the hub **`task/sv0c-runtime-executable.Rmd`**. This file is a
**living index** — flip status as slices land and keep it aligned with the
hub's phase narrative. No implementation has started (confirmed by repo audit
2026-08-23: only the test-convenience `./scripts/sv0 compile-run` exists); every
slice below is `todo`.

## how to use

- Pick the next slice by band (F0 → F0/R0 → R0 → R0.1 → R1); within a band
  slices are ordered by dependency exactly as spec §30.2 lists them.
- Each slice names the spec **requirement ID(s)** it implements and the exact
  **red test / acceptance** signal from spec §31. Cite the requirement and
  acceptance ID (`AC-0##`) in the implementation PR (spec Appendix D
  traceability rule).
- Every slice follows the spec's five-state cycle (§30.1): **Contract → Red →
  Minimal green → Adversarial expansion → Refactor and evidence**. A slice is
  not done at "minimal green" — filesystem/process/path/runtime-selection/
  publication slices require the adversarial-expansion state too.
- Use the fake emitter (§26.2) and fake C compiler (§26.3) contracts for every
  slice before wiring a real host compiler in; this is what lets PIPE/SEC
  tests run without rebuilding the self-hosted compiler per case.
- Add a one-line result + commit/PR when a slice lands, same convention as the
  M4 checklist (`task/sv0-toolchain-milestone-4-checklist.Rmd`).
- Reset `/tmp/.sv0_drv_path` to empty before any gate/push that touches this
  area, and never run these driver scripts concurrently with a pre-push
  `sv0 test` until NEX-011 retires the global control file from this path —
  see `[[feedback_drv_path_reset]]`.

### F0/R0 — core compiler and entry ABI (spec §31.2)

| NEX-011 | Add a reentrant core-compiler request interface; retire the global control file from the stable path | REL-004 | **done (migration shim — see note)** | `scripts/native_exe_core_compiler.py` — `CoreCompilerClient`/`CoreCompilerRequest`, a POSIX-`flock`-serialized wrapper around the legacy `/tmp/.sv0_drv_path` binary (spec §22.2's explicitly sanctioned migration mechanism, **not** the stable reentrant ABI AE-008 ultimately requires). Investigated the real fix first: sv0 has no argv/CLI-args host function at all — the native compiler's CLI entry is synthesized at build time by `scripts/build-sv0-megatu-native.sh` string-injecting a `/tmp/.sv0_drv_path` read into generated sv0 source, because `read_file(path)` is the only external-input channel the language has. A real fix needs a new host function across resolver/checker/C-lowering/runtime (+ `sv0doc`, which owns language capabilities) — scoped out as its own future slice, not done here. 4-case `--selftest`: (1) demonstrates real cross-contamination *without* the lock via a fake compiler that reads-then-sleeps-then-echoes the control file (widens the race window deterministically; stable across 15 repeated runs); (2) 6 concurrent requests through the real `CoreCompilerClient.invoke()` are always correctly isolated; (3) control-file format builders match `scripts/sv0`'s own `run_compile`/`run_emit_verified` exactly; (4) control file is always reset to empty after `invoke()`. Wired into `sv0 test-guards`. Verified load-bearing: removing the `flock` call reproduces cross-contamination in 10/10 runs. **Known limitation, documented in the module docstring**: this lock only protects concurrent calls made *through this module* — an unrelated `scripts/sv0` subcommand or the self-host loop touching the control file outside this protocol can still race against it. |

Wired into `sv0 test-guards`. Verified load-bearing by mutation: checking stdout emptiness before exit code (the exact ordering bug PIPE-003 exists to prevent) fails the `partial` case. |

### Traceability audit — citation hygiene + closed gaps (2026-08-27)

Step 2 of the post-R1 traceability plan (step 1: fix the guard itself,
above): a real per-ID audit of all 25 requirements
`verify_native_exe_traceability.py --active-release R1` flagged after the
guard fix. Each was checked against actual code/tests, not assumed —
either cited where real, already-tested coverage existed but was never
properly recorded (citation-hygiene fixes, added directly to the rows
above), or closed with real new work (below), or recorded as a genuine,
still-open gap (also below, none silently dropped).

**Root cause found for most of the CLI-0xx gaps**: NEX-059's own section
header used `CLI-007/008/010…013/017` — a compact shorthand that
`extract_cited_ids`'s regex cannot actually parse (each id after the
first needs its own `PREFIX-` letters; a bare `/008` has no prefix to
attach to). This meant CLI-008/010/011/012/013/017 were **never actually
cited**, even before the citation-context bug fix — a second, independent
mistake compounding the first. Fixed by rewriting the header as
`CLI-007, CLI-008, CLI-010…013, CLI-017` (the same comma-separated
convention every other multi-id header already uses), which the guard
parses correctly.

**Citation-hygiene fixes** (real, already-tested coverage found and
cited, no new code): `TOOL-011` → NEX-003, `SEC-007` → NEX-028,
`PIPE-010` → NEX-012, `PORT-003` → NEX-010, `SEC-010` → NEX-020,
`CLI-011` → NEX-021, `SEC-008` → NEX-024 (with a stated caveat: absence +
env hardening, not an active deny-test), `CLI-012` → NEX-027, `ENTRY-009`
→ NEX-031, `PORT-002` → NEX-038, `GOV-006` → NEX-042, `TEST-003` →
NEX-037, `PIPE-012` → NEX-053, `SEC-011` → NEX-056a (with a stated
caveat: licenses ship as real files, just not cross-referenced inside the
same JSON bundle), `GOV-009` → NEX-057. See each row above for the exact
evidence.

**Genuine gaps closed in this pass** (real new code, not just citation):
- `CLI-008` (file mode must be a regular, readable `.sv0` file — missing/
  directory/FIFO/wrong-extension all fail cleanly): new
  `scripts/native_exe_input_validation.py` — `validate_file_input_shape`,
  wired as the very first check in `build_native_executable`, before
  `validate_entry_exists`'s own raw `open()` call. 7-case `--selftest`
  (missing file, directory, FIFO, wrong extension, unreadable file — the
  last two skip gracefully on a platform/user that can't exercise them).
  This also closes the previously-flagged follow-up task about
  `validate_entry_exists` crashing with a raw `FileNotFoundError` instead
  of a clean `BuildError`. Wired into `sv0 test-guards`; `native_exe_build.py`
  gained its own case 8 proving the same thing end to end through the
  full pipeline. Verified load-bearing by mutation on both modules:
  removing the regular-file check, and removing the wiring call entirely,
  are each caught immediately.
- `CLI-013` (`--verbose` exposes normalized, non-secret build detail):
  `--verbose` was parsed by `native_exe_cli.py` and carried all the way
  into `NativeBuildRequest.verbose`, but **`native_exe_main.py` never
  read it at all** — a real, silent dead flag, found by direct code
  review (its sibling `--quiet` was correctly wired; `--verbose` was
  overlooked). Fixed: a new `_format_verbose_detail` in `native_exe_main.py`
  prints input/output/profile/contract-mode/compiler identity and a
  reconstructed host-compiler argv shape (via `native_exe_human_output.render_argv_for_display`,
  which existed, tested, and was never called by anything before this).
  New selftest case 9 confirms `--verbose` output actually appears.

  immediately.

**Genuine gaps left open, honestly, not fixed in this pass** (real,
scoped, but out of the size this pass should rush):
- `GOV-007` — conflicts among language spec/compiler/runtime tracked and
  blocking affected release claims. No issue/waiver-tracking mechanism
  exists anywhere in this project.
- `REPRO-001` — project-mode file ordering and emitted C determinism.

  project-mode determinism test exists.
- `SEC-012` — a reviewed threat model and security contact per stable

- `TEST-005` — a systematic "every error phase has a negative test"

- `TOOL-013` — supported compiler families/versions pinned as a declared

New `scripts/native_exe_harness_env.py` — `verify_harness_env` (injectable env/umask for tests) is the check that a future edit to that wrapper can't silently drop the pinning; `_current_umask` reads the real umask via the standard POSIX read-then-restore trick, verified in its own case to never permanently change it. 6-case `--selftest`, plus a `--verify` mode run live at the very start of `run_python_guards` against the real, just-pinned environment. Verified load-bearing by mutation: neutering the raise is caught by 4 of the 6 cases at once. |

### NEX-062 — Section 17: wire `sv0.toml` into `normalize_request`

User-requested follow-up after "is the sv0c runtime spec fully
implemented?" surfaced `sv0.toml` as one of the real, known gaps: the
config module (NEX-043) was fully built and tested in isolation, but
nothing ever called it from a real build.

| ID | slice | status | red test / acceptance |
|----|-------|--------|-----------|
| NEX-062 | Wire `native_exe_config.discover_config`/`load_config`/`resolve_precedence` into `native_exe_request.normalize_request` for all six `[build]` keys (`profile`, `contract-mode`, `c-compiler`, `output-dir`, `keep-c`, `build-record`), per §11.4's CLI > config > default precedence and §17.4's config-file-relative path rules. | **done** | `native_exe_request.py`: discovery runs once `input_path` is absolute (§17.3: beside the file, or `<project>/sv0.toml`); a new `_tier` helper maps this module's `None` ("not given") onto `resolve_precedence`'s `_UNSET` sentinel, since a real CLI/config value is never legitimately `None` for any of these six keys. `c-compiler`/`output-dir` config values are resolved against the **config file's own directory** before ever competing in the precedence tier (§17.4), never cwd — CLI's own `-o`/`--cc` values are untouched by this resolution and still win outright. A malformed `sv0.toml` raises `RequestError`, matching how an unrecognized `--profile`/`--contract-mode` value already fails. `native_exe_cli.ParsedArgs.profile`/`.contract_mode` changed from string defaults (`"dev"`/`"runtime"`) to `None`, since the old design had no way to distinguish "not given" from "explicitly given the same value as the default" — required for genuine CLI-vs-config precedence to be checkable at all (confirmed no existing case in either module's corpus depended on the old string defaults, so this cost zero regressions). `native_exe_output_path._stem_for` promoted to public `stem_for` (needed for the config-`output-dir` default-path computation). 21-case `--selftest` (up from 13): 8 new cases against a real `sv0.toml` on disk — config supplies profile/contract-mode/c-compiler/output-dir/keep-c/build-record when the CLI doesn't, CLI still wins over config for profile and `--cc`, config's `c-compiler`/`output-dir` resolve against the config file's directory (verified with cwd genuinely different from the config directory, so a wrong-base mutation cannot pass by coincidence), and a malformed config raises `RequestError`. `native_exe_main.py` gained a 10th real end-to-end selftest case: a real `sv0.toml` (`contract-mode = "disabled"`) beside a real fixture, built with **zero CLI flags**, produces exit 8 (the check stripped) instead of exit 1 (the check aborting) — proving the wiring through the entire pipeline, not just `normalize_request` in isolation. `config_path` (already an existing, previously-always-`None` field) is now real, and surfaced in `--verbose` output and in build records (`native_exe_build_record.py`'s existing `config` parameter, previously never populated), per §17.3's own text ("the selected configuration path appears in verbose output and build records"). **Manually verified end to end**: a real `sv0.toml` with `profile = "release"` / `contract-mode = "disabled"` drove a real build with no CLI flags at all — the release argv shape (`-O2 -fno-strict-aliasing`) and exit 8 both appeared exactly as configured. Wired into `sv0 test-guards`. Verified load-bearing by 6 separate mutations: swapping CLI/config precedence order, resolving `c-compiler`/`output-dir` against cwd instead of the config directory (twice), silently swallowing a `ConfigError`, hardcoding `keep_c_requested` to the CLI flag alone, and collapsing the `CcSelection.EXPLICIT`/`.CONFIG` distinction — every one caught. **Deliberately not done, stated honestly**: the `SV0_CC` environment-variable tier (`native_exe_cc_select.py`'s own docstring names it as a separate, still-unimplemented R0.1 tier) — this slice wires the `sv0.toml` tier only, since that's what was asked. `native-executable.md`'s prior "genuinely unwired" note corrected in the same pass. |

### NEX-063 — CLI-014: wire `--emit=c` into both CLI surfaces

User-requested follow-up after "wire sv0.toml into normalize_request" —
`--emit=c` (`native_exe_emit_c.emit_c_only`, NEX-039) was fully built and
tested, but `native_exe_cli.py`'s grammar unconditionally rejected it.

| ID | slice | status | red test / acceptance |
|----|-------|--------|-----------|
| NEX-063 | Accept `--emit=c` on both CLI surfaces, dispatch to `emit_c_only` instead of `build_native_executable`, and enforce its documented contract (an explicit `-o`, no `--keep-c`/`--build-record`/`--message-format=json`). | **done** | `native_exe_cli.py`: `ParsedArgs.emit_value` ("exe"\|"c", replacing the old exe-only `--emit` rejection); parse-time enforcement of `emit_c_only`'s own documented contract — `--emit=c` requires an explicit `-o` (no default-naming rule exists for it), and rejects `--keep-c`/`--build-record`/`--message-format=json` in combination (none has a coherent meaning with no executable artifact or compiler identity). 5 new/changed cases (35 total, up from 30). `native_exe_request.py`: new `Emit.C_ONLY`, normalized from `parsed.emit_value`. `native_exe_emit_c.py`: gained the same CLI-008 file-input-shape hardening (`validate_file_input_shape`) `build_native_executable` already has, closing a parity gap this slice's own investigation surfaced (a missing file under `--emit=c` would otherwise leak a raw `OSError`) — 4-case selftest (up from 3). `native_exe_human_output.py`: new `format_emit_c_success_message` (`"sv0c: wrote C to <path>"`, deliberately distinct in shape from the executable-build success line, since no backend/profile/contracts ever apply). `native_exe_main.py`: an early dispatch on `request.emit` calls `emit_c_only` instead of `build_native_executable`, honoring `--quiet`/`--verbose` the same way the executable path does. 4 new real end-to-end selftest cases (14 total, up from 10): a real `--emit=c` write with real emitted-C content checks, a bare `--emit=c` (no `-o`) usage error, `--emit=c` + `--keep-c` rejected, and `--quiet` suppressing `--emit=c`'s own output. **Manually verified end to end on both CLI surfaces** (`./scripts/sv0 native-compile --emit=c` and the installed `sv0c --emit=c`, via a real `build_install_layout`+`write_sv0c_launcher` tree): both wrote real, correct C; the `-o`-required and invalid-`--emit`-value usage errors both produced exit 2 with the expected messages. Wired into `sv0 test-guards`. Verified load-bearing by mutation: each of the 3 new CLI-parse checks (missing `-o`, `--keep-c` combination, `--message-format=json` combination) is caught individually by its own case; the `native_exe_main.py` dispatch itself is caught by a mutation that routes `--emit=c` through the executable-build path instead (a real crash trying to read a binary as text, not a silent pass); `native_exe_emit_c.py`'s new hardening call is caught the same way `native_exe_input_validation.py`'s own mutation already proved for the executable path. |

### NEX-064 — TOOL-001…002: implement the `SV0_CC` environment-variable tier

User-requested follow-up closing the last known wiring gap in the
compiler-selection precedence — `native_exe_cc_select.py`'s own docstring
had named `SV0_CC` as a distinct R0.1 tier since NEX-021, never implemented.

| ID | slice | status | red test / acceptance |
|----|-------|--------|-----------|
| NEX-064 | Insert `SV0_CC` as a real tier between the unified explicit (`--cc`/`sv0.toml`) tier and `CC`, completing the spec's own stated 5-tier order (`--cc → sv0.toml → SV0_CC → CC → PATH`). | **done** | `native_exe_cc_select.py`: new `CcSelection.SV0_CC_ENV`; a shared `_resolve_env_var` helper (factored out of the pre-existing `CC` handling, used identically for both `SV0_CC` and `CC` — same resolution rule, same fail-closed-on-invalid-value behavior, no duplicated logic). `select_cc` checks `SV0_CC` before `CC`; an unset `SV0_CC` falls through to `CC`, but a SET-and-invalid `SV0_CC` is a hard `TOOL_DISCOVERY` error, never a silent skip to `CC` (matching `CC`'s own pre-existing behavior — "falls through" means absent, not invalid, a distinction now stated explicitly in the module's own docstring). No changes needed anywhere else: `native_exe_build.py` already calls `select_cc(explicit_cc, os.environ)`, so `SV0_CC` is picked up automatically once `select_cc` itself checks for it. 5 new cases (11 total, up from 6): `SV0_CC` wins over `CC` when both are set, `SV0_CC` alone resolves correctly, an invalid `SV0_CC` is a hard error even with a perfectly valid `CC` present, and an explicit `--cc`/`sv0.toml` value still wins outright over `SV0_CC`. **Manually verified end to end on both CLI surfaces** (`./scripts/sv0 native-compile` and a real installed `sv0c` binary, freshly rebuilt to pick up this change): `SV0_CC` pointed at a real wrapper compiler while `CC=/usr/bin/false` was also set — the build succeeded using the `SV0_CC` wrapper, `--verbose` correctly reported its identity, and `CC`'s deliberately broken value was never reached. Wired into `sv0 test-guards` (same line as NEX-021). Verified load-bearing by mutation: removing the `SV0_CC` check entirely is caught immediately (a real crash on the "SV0_CC alone" case, since nothing else resolves); swapping `SV0_CC`'s and `CC`'s check order is caught by both the precedence-order case and the invalid-value case. **With this slice, the sv0c native-executable driver's compiler-selection precedence is fully implemented — all five spec-defined tiers are real, tested, and wired.** |

## dependency notes (spec §30.2, condensed)

Slices within a band are already dependency-ordered above; across bands, the
load-bearing chain is: CLI/state-machine (NEX-001…003) → fake harnesses
(NEX-004…005) → publication + scratch abstractions (NEX-007…008) → argv
subprocess + VM rejection (NEX-009…010) → reentrant core-compiler interface
(NEX-011, retires the global control file) → entry ABI (NEX-013…018) → one
real single-file link (first real-`cc` slice inside NEX-019…023) → runtime
feature/behavior-corpus migration (NEX-028…029) → project mode (NEX-030) →
contract-mode matrix (NEX-031) → hostile paths/symlinks/cancellation/parallel
builds (NEX-033…036) → platform matrix + installed-layout (NEX-037, NEX-046)
→ retained-C/JSON/config/provenance (NEX-039…047) → UB/warnings/release
profile (NEX-048…051) → same-output locking + reproducibility (NEX-052…053)
→ stable ABI + release evidence + doc publication + recipe de-duplication
(NEX-054…058).
